title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
The Flora City Council met Monday afternoon for their second meeting of the month.  But, before the meeting was called to order, a public hearing was held.  It’s purpose was to garner support for a grant proposal that could result in the award of millions of dollars for new sidewalks in Flora.

City leaders made a push to invite the public to voice their opinion and their support for the effort that, if approved, would see sidewalks on Vincennes Avenue from South Mill Street to the Industrial Park, South Stanford Road, Commercial Drive, Industrial Parkway and Briscoe Drive.  Their effort to seek public input paid off in spades, as over twenty people attended to learn more.  Mitch Hardiek of Milano and Grunloh Engineers of Effingham explained the process of applying for the ITEP (Illinois Transportation Enhancement Program) Grant that can supply 100% grant funding for the project which is estimated to cost $3.1 Million.  It seeks to install 2.5 miles of five foot wide ADA compliant sidewalks in Flora as well as correcting some storm sewer issues.  Consensus seemed to favor support for the overall project but it also raised questions about replacing sidewalks in other parts of town that have become dangerous or are not truly suitable for safe passage near heavily trafficked areas.  There were also requests for warning lights and pedestrian crossings at several places in town.  It was pointed out how dangerous it can be with even fatal results from trying to traverse areas on Vincennes and South Stanford with narrow streets and deep ditches to contend with.  Mayor Linda Spicer and others thanked everyone for coming and voicing their opinion and support for the grant application.  More than one person thanked commissioners for their effort to improve the city in this regard.  People were encouraged to sign the petition to show their support and some asked if they should write letters of support.  City Administrator Mike Stanford said those kinds of letters are the most beneficial, specifically when the letters are handwritten and include a signature.  Those letters have the most impact.  Printed letters with a signature and emails are also sought as well as pictures of problem areas in the proposed construction area.  Teachers were also encouraged to ask students to write letters of support for the project.  Those items should all be brought to Flora City Hall before the submission deadline in October.  After everyone had a chance to voice their remarks, Mayor Spicer thanked everyone for coming and brought the hearing to a close.

The mayor then called the regular meeting order and open the floor to public comment.  Arriel Dulaney with the Flora Chamber of Commerce spoke briefly to ask for street closures for the former Moonlight Madness event that has been relabeled Fall into Flora and will stretch over two days on November 6 and 7.  It will be focused on W. North Ave. and Main St as well as Gaslight Square.  Commissioners approved her request without dissent.  Next, Stephen Smith with Flora Tourism spoke about the fifth Ford Town event that is planned for September 18 and 19 in downtown Flora.  It includes a Cruise In Friday from 5-8pm and the car show on Saturday.  Last year 90 vehicles were shown and more are expected this year.  Smith says the Flora Community Market will be part of the event as well as inflatables, craft vendors and a growing Chili Cook Off that also includes craft brewers.  Smith also informed the council that the Flora Kriskindle Market for 2026 is planned for December 11 and 12. The council approved his request with instructions to Smith and Dulaney to confer with Flora Police about working out the logistics.

Next, the Flora City Council approved the meeting agenda and the consent agenda.  The latter included the approval of past meeting minutes, the Police Activity Report, Building and Zoning Report and Treasurers Report for July as well as the warrant list for the first half of August.

In regular business, Mayor Linda Spicer said she wanted to congratulate and help to celebrate a Flora High School Student who has excelled and earned high accolades.  She recognized Paul Hudson for winning the Microsoft Excel National Tournament in Nashville in June and then went on to the global competition where he finished fourth.  Spicer also congratulated Alicia Westjohn for the success of  her students at these high-level events.  The mayor then asked for commissioners to approve a resolution to allow certain employees to attend the Illinois Municipal League Annual Meeting in Chicago September 17-19.  The measure was unanimously approved.

Mayor Spicer then turned to commissioners for their comments.  Commissioner Phil Wiley offered condolences to the family of Commissioner Jeremy Henderson over the loss of his Grandfather Larry Henderson.  Wiley also reminded everyone that football season is underway with Flora JFL picking up two wins this past Saturday.  Also the Flora Wolves open their season Friday night at 7:00 at Dancey Field when they play the Sesser-Valier Red Devils.

Flora City Administrator/Economic Development Director Mike Stanford presented five items for commissioners consideration.  First, the council unanimously approved an ordinance granting a sewer line easement for Matt Winterrowd on North State Street.  Next, Stanford asked commissioners to approve an ordinance for an agreement with the South Central Illinois Regional Planning and Development Commission.  SCIRP-DC assists communities in south central Illinois in applying for various grants and other governmental programs.  Their staff greatly improves the likelihood of securing approval of the funding they seek.  The ordinance sets a rate of $50 per hour with a cap not to exceed $5,000.  The measure passed 4-1 with Commissioner Jeremy Henderson voting No.  Next commissioners approved two payments to the Illinois Municipal League Risk Management Association for above the maximum claim allowed.  One overage was for contract year 2023 in the amount of $21,773 and the other overage was for contract year 2024 in the amount of $14,232.

Flora City Clerk Kaci O’Dell announced that petitions are available for the position of Mayor of the City of Flora and for Commissioners beginning August 26 at Flora City Hall from 9:00am-4:30pm.  Petittions are due back by November 23.  The election is April 6, 2027.

Superintendent of Public Services Toby Rinehart sought approval of two items.  Rinehart asked commissioners to approve a resolution for maintenance under the Illinois Highway Code for MFT Fund for Oil and Chipping of Flora streets at a cost of $190,000.  The measure was approved unanimously.  Commissioners were also asked to approve the hiring of Robert Henson as a Swing Shift Waste Water Treatment Operator at a rate of $35.38 per hour, effective August 31.  The motion was approved without dissent.  With all business complete, the meeting adjourned.

title: MONDAY ACCIDENT
full_story:
Illinois State Police Troop 9 were called to the scene of a serious traffic crash on US Route 50 at Big Four Road at about 5:30 am Monday.

According to initial reports the accident involved an ISP Trooper Squad Car and a Semi.  State Police say the Trooper was transported to an area hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.  The roadway was shut down for approximately 7 hours and reopened at approximately 12:10 pm.

Additional information on the crash has not yet been released.

title: FLORA SCHOOL BOARD
full_story:
The Board recognized Hayden Young and Paul Hudson for their outstanding achievements at the Certiport Microsoft Suite competitions.  Hayden placed fifth in Microsoft Word at the national competition.  Paul Hudson was the National Champion in Microsoft Excel and placed fourth at the World Championships.

The board approved the tentative budget and set a public hearing for September 21 during the regular board meeting.  The board also approved the bid for the purchase of a used school bus submitted by John Upton.

In personnel matters the board employed Terri Kautz as part-time special education teacher at Floyd Henson Junior High School, Shelby Hoagland and Haley Gonzalezas as paraprofessionals, Emma Kitley as Guidance Secretary, and Isham Lusk as full-time custodian substitute.  Approved Kelsey Cox as assistant junior high softball coach, Colleen Steber and Alice Shales as volunteer assistants for high school band.  The board also accepted the resignation as 6th Grade Girls’ basketball coach submitted by Chris Krutsinger and Robin Price effective August 10th.

title: PETITIONS AVAILABLE
full_story:
Flora City Clerk Kaci O’Dell announced that petition forms and other applicable election filing forms for the office of Mayor and Commissioners for the City of Flora will be available to interested, qualified, registered voters beginning Tuesday, August 25th.  The packet of forms and pertinent information may be picked up at Flora City Hall, 131 East Second Street, Monday through Friday, between the hours of 9:00 am and 4:30 pm, with the exception of holiday closures.

Flora’s Consolidated Election, to be held on April 6th, and will be for electing a Mayor and four Commissioners.  Individuals elected will serve a 4-year term, beginning May 1st (first regular council meeting of May) through April 30, 2031.  If petitions filed total more than four for the Mayor’s position and/or more than sixteen for the Commissioners’ positions, a Consolidated Primary Election will be held on February 23rd.

Prospective candidates may start circulating petitions on August 25th.

The filing period for nonpartisan candidates is November 16th through November 23rd.

A notice will be circulated to the media as a reminder of the filing dates.

title: FLORA POLICE ACTIVITY REPORT
full_story:
Flora Chief of Jeremy Ruger released his Activity Report for July during Monday’s Flora City Council meeting.

During the month, Flora police officers investigated five traffic accidents.

They made seven criminal arrests.  There were two drug arrests and two DUI arrests during July.  There were three local ordinance arrests, 18 traffic arrests and five warrant arrests.

Officers issued 36 warning tickets, responded to 11 alarms and had 1,254 calls for service and had no juvenile contacts.

Also, Flora police officers drove 4,137 miles and conducted 94 investigations during July.  They answered 343, 911 calls and conducted eight UTV Inspections and two Golf Cart Inspections during July.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
Statewide, the USDA says 59% of the corn crop is in good to excellent condition, with 98% silking, 82% in dough stage, 31% dented, and 1% mature, while 59% of soybeans are in good shape with 94% blooming and 85% setting pods.

According to the USDA there were 3.3 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending August 16th.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 4% very short, 15% short, 56% adequate, and 25% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 5% very short, 18% short, 61% adequate, and 16% surplus.

Corn Silking reached 98% equal to the 5-year average.  Corn dough reached 82%, compared to the 5-year average of 78%.  Corn dented reached 31%, compared to the 5-year average of 29%.  Corn mature reached 1%.  Corn condition was rated 3% very poor, 8% poor, 30% fair, 46% good, and 13% excellent.

Soybeans blooming reached 94%, compared to the 5-year average of 95%.  Soybeans setting pods reached 85%, compared to the 5-year average of 82%.  Soybeans condition was rated 3% very poor, 7% poor, 31% fair, 47% good, and 12% excellent.

title: FLORA BUILDING AND ZONING REPORT
full_story:
Flora Building and Zoning Official Chad Bayles presented the monthly building and zoning report for July during Monday’s Flora City Council meeting.

The report shows two new residential construction projects were undertaken in July, valued at $6,500.

And there were no new industrial projects started during July.

There were two total new projects in Flora for July, valued at $6,500 with $110 collected in permit fees and $100 in deposit fees collected for July

The year-to-date figures show 41 total residential projects so far this year with a value of $591,620.

There are four year-to-date commercial projects valued at $17,444,334 and no new industrial projects.

That makes 45 total projects valued at $18,035,954, with $2,373 in permit fees and $700 in deposit fees collected for the year.

title: MISSING MAN FOUND
full_story:
A Mt. Vernon Dementia patient reported missing Sunday night was found safe early Monday morning.  83-year-old William Downey from a Mt. Vernon nursing home was found safe in the old emergency room of Deaconess Illinois Crossroads Hospital.

Mt. Vernon Assistant Fire Chief, Bryan Jennings says a search began for the patient when the nursing home determined he was missing from the facility around seven Sunday night.  The search had to be discontinued five hours later around midnight due to storms moving into the area.

Around four Monday morning, police were notified the man had been found sitting in a seat at the old emergency room of Crossroads Hospital.  He had told police he was waiting for the cleaning crew.  It was not clear how he had gotten into the closed off section of the hospital.

The search was conducted by Mt. Vernon city police and fire along with Jefferson County Fire and EMS.

The name of the nursing home involved has not been released by Mt. Vernon fire officials.
